meta.author: Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur
meta.first_line: gāite gāite nāma ki daśā ha-ila

title: Śrī Śikṣāṣṭakam
author: by Śrī Chaitanya Mahāprabhu in Sanskrit
subtitle: Verse Seven

translation: “O Govinda! Without You, the world is empty. Tears are flooding my eyes like rain, and a moment seems like forever.”
*Corresponding Bengali composition by Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur:*

text: gāite gāite nāma ki daśā ha-ila
translation: Chanting the Name again and again, what was my condition? Within my heart I realised, “I am an eternal servant of Kṛṣṇa.”
I realised that I was bound by Māyā’s ropes in this dull mundane universe, and I simply experience misery in various ways due to separation from Lord Govinda.

text: āra ye saṁsāra mora nāhi lāge bhāla
kā̐hā yāi’ kṛṣṇa heri e chintā viśāla
translation: And I don’t much like this world of birth and death. Where shall I go to see Kṛṣṇa? This was my biggest worry.
I began weeping and weeping; my tears fell. Torrents of rain poured from my eyes just like the rains of the monsoon season.
Now, a moment for me is like a hundred ages. I cannot bear this separation from Lord Govinda.

text: ki kari ki kari    sthira nāhi haya
translation: The world is empty; as I survey the four directions, the entire surface of the world is void. My life is empty, my mind is listless; I am indifferent and apathetic towards everything. Depressed, melancholy and forlorn, my life has no meaning now. What do I do now? I cannot remain steady. I can no longer maintain my life.
O residents of Vṛndāvan, save my life and show me Rādhānāth, the Lord of Śrī Rādhā. Considering this humble prayer of Bhakti Vinod, please give him Your association and take him with You.

text: parāṇa chhāḍite āra dina dui chāri
translation: I am unable to further tolerate this separation from my Lord Kṛṣṇa and am ready to give up my life within a few days (lit. two or four days).
